stem: A 56-year-old woman is evaluated for fatigue and dyspnea on exertion.  Medical history includes hypertension and systemic sclerosis.  Blood pressure is 135/80 mm Hg and pulse is 68/min.  Cardiac examination demonstrates a loud S2 with no murmurs.  Lungs are clear to auscultation.  The patient undergoes right heart catheterization, during which a balloon-tipped catheter is advanced into the pulmonary artery.  The balloon occludes a branch of the pulmonary artery, and the pressure beyond the point of occlusion is measured.  At this point in the procedure, the measured pressure most closely reflects which of the following?​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​
explanation:
Pulmonary artery catheterization (also called Swan-Ganz or right heart catheterization) is used to diagnose pulmonary hypertension and occasionally to manage patients who are critically ill.  During the procedure, a catheter is inserted into the systemic venous system, and a small balloon at the distal tip of the catheter is inflated with saline.  The catheter is then delivered to the heart, where it is advanced through the right atrium, right ventricle, and pulmonary artery and finally lodged in a branch of the pulmonary artery.  The inflated balloon temporarily occludes forward flow, leaving a static column of blood that is continuous with the pulmonary capillaries and veins and therefore transmits pressure from the left atrium.  The pressure measured at the catheter tip at this time is called the pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), and it closely reflects left atrial pressure and left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP).

(Choices A and C)  Direct measurement of intrapleural pressure (pleural manometry) can be obtained by placing a catheter in the pleural space during thoracentesis, whereas mean airway pressure can be measured during mechanical ventilation.  Pulmonary artery catheterization does not measure intrapleural or mean airway pressures.

(Choice D)  Mean arterial pressure is measured by placing an arterial catheter directly in the central arterial circulation (eg, common femoral or radial artery).  It reflects the average aortic pressure.

(Choice E)  Pulse pressure is the difference between systemic arterial systolic and diastolic blood pressures.

(Choices F and G)  Right atrial pressure and right ventricular systolic pressure can be measured directly during right heart catheterization by placing the catheter in the respective chambers.  The left-sided heart chambers cannot be directly accessed during right heart catheterization (the catheter cannot pass through the pulmonary capillaries), but PCWP serves as an accurate reflection of left atrial pressure and LVEDP.

Educational objective:Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) is measured at the distal tip of a pulmonary artery catheter after an inflated balloon occludes blood flow through a pulmonary artery branch.  PCWP closely approximates left atrial pressure and left ventricular end-diastolic pressure.​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​
